all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Canada's innovation strategy, organised into four key areas (knowledge performance, skills performance, innovation environment, and community-based innovation), with specific targets by 2010 including ranking among the top five countries in R&D performance, doubling government R&D investment, and developing at least 10 internationally recognised technology clusters.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: The strategy aims to increase public and private R&D investment, develop skilled labour, and create innovation clusters, all of which support productivity growth and innovation capacity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The strategy was organised into four key areas with goals and targets, and a 2004 assessment of progress was commissioned from the Conference Board of Canada.

It represents a major structural commitment to innovation policy across multiple dimensions.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Canada's innovation strategy has been organised into four key areas each with goals and specific targets. These are set out below, along with the first assessment, in 2004, of progress towards meeting them.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The government's National Science Advisor proposed a framework for evaluating and prioritising proposals for major science investments and overseeing the management of those projects, emphasising the need for a clearly articulated, integrated national science and technology policy.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The OECD recommends examining whether the efficiency of the SR&ED (Scientific Research and Experimental Development) tax credits might be improved, including exploring options to redesign them to target R&D in new firms and encourage incremental spending on R&D.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The OECD recommends eliminating federal and provincial tax credits for investments in Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations (LSVCCs) so they compete on the same basis as other venture capital funds.

all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: Eliminating the federal and provincial tax credits for investments in Labour-Sponsored Venture Capital Corporations so that they are required to compete on the same basis as other venture capital funds.
